items.title: Connor Hellebuyck speaks to media in 1st return to Winnipeg since forcing trade from Jets
items.summary_auto: Connor Hellebuyck will face the media — but not his former teammates or Jets fans — when he returns to Winnipeg for the first time since his trade to the New Jersey Devils.

items.title: Nvidia and CEO Jensen Huang face lawsuit over handling of ties to alleged Chinese spy
items.summary_auto: The lawsuit filed in San Jose, Calif., on Monday accuses the CEO and his company of misleading shareholders by concealing the relationship with a woman accused of feeding information to Bejing, and not disclosing that the matter raised national security concerns ‌that threatened Nvidia's reputation and business prospects.

items.title: Defiant Hegseth calls Republican's impeachment resolution a 'farce'
items.summary_auto: U.S. Secretary of War Pete Hegseth condemned a resolution in the House of Representatives calling for his impeachment, describing it as a "farce" from a "disgruntled congressman" who is leaving office.

items.title: Anthropic eyes $1 trillion US valuation in hotly anticipated IPO that's a key test for AI market
items.summary_auto: Anthropic's initial public offering  plans to raise as much as $64.4 billion US, a regulatory filing showed on Tuesday, testing Wall Street's faith in the AI boom amid growing worries about its risks.

items.title: Amid sky-high oilpatch profits, Alberta's premier wants to offer oil companies a new subsidy. Here's why
Hamilton, 3 other expansion PWHL teams reveal names and logos ahead of inaugural season
items.summary_auto: Hamilton Havoc, Detroit Clutch, San Jose Sea Lions and Vegas Vanguards will begin play this upcoming season. All four now have logos, but they won't appear on the teams' jerseys until the 2027-28 season.

items.title: Canada reimposes sanctions on Iran for violating nuclear non-proliferation commitments
items.summary_auto: Canada is reimposing sanctions on 11 Iranian energy and financial organizations for the regime's failure to meet promises related to its nuclear program, its ballistic missile development and its ongoing financing of violence beyond its borders.

items.title: More than 250 mm of rain forecast for some B.C. areas as storm makes landfall
items.summary_auto: The B.C. River Forecast Centre has issued flood watches for the South Coast, Vancouver Island and river basins in the Central Coast and Fraser Valley.

items.title: Ukrainian conscription in the crosshairs
items.summary_auto: A riot outside Kyiv may have been sparked by false claims — but it is highlighting tensions over Ukraine’s forced conscription methods.

items.title: Specialized burn treatments deployed for soldiers injured in Alberta military base fire
items.summary_auto: In Alberta, 21 soldiers remain in hospital, with nine in critical condition, according to a provincial health agency. Fifteen of those patients are on ventilators to help them breathe.

items.title: Manitoba volunteers search for unmarked veterans' graves to make sure all get proper headstones
items.summary_auto: Brandon's George MacKay volunteers with the Last Post Fund, a non-profit that works to add headstones to the graves of veterans buried without one. "You can't just let them be on their own," says MacKay. "They got to be recognized."

items.title: These domestic violence shelters can hardly keep up with the cost of groceries
items.summary_auto: As the cost of living and the price of groceries continue to soar, the people who run domestic violence shelters for women and children are struggling to keep up.

items.title: U.S.-mediated talks between Russia and Ukraine begin in Abu Dhabi
items.summary_auto: Three-way talks between Russia, Ukraine and the United States opened Tuesday in the United Arab Emirates, as Washington made another push to end the war that followed  Moscow's all-out invasion of its neighbour nearly five years ago.

items.title: N.L. man could be barred from entering U.S. due to Trump Facebook comment
items.summary_auto: A man in St. John’s, N.L., could be barred from ever travelling south of the border after the U.S. Secret Service flagged a Facebook comment he doesn’t even remember making against President Donald Trump.

items.title: Where Trump goes now on the big 3: tariffs, Iran war, immigration
items.summary_auto: After his party's calamitous loss in the midterms, a looming question is whether U.S. President Donald Trump will shift course on any of his three biggest initiatives since returning to the White House: tariffs, the war with Iran and immigration enforcement.

items.title: Lions and tigers are kept legally in Ontario backyards. No one knows how many there are
items.summary_auto: Lions and tigers are among some of the most recognizable and dangerous predators in the world. They're also legal to own in Ontario, where provincial authorities can't say how many are being held in private cages and backyards.

items.title: Military budget squeeze limits paid Remembrance Day participation in Ontario
items.summary_auto: Despite billions in new defence spending, military budget restraints are limiting paid Remembrance Day participation in southwestern Ontario. Leaked emails reveal commanders capped attendance at 50 reservists per unit, prompting complaints from troops. The military says soldiers can still attend ceremonies in uniform, but without being paid.

items.title: Why health care for Canadian women veterans is falling short
items.summary_auto: Women are the fastest growing segment of Canada’s veteran population, but they have complex physical and mental health problems that often get treated in isolation. A report released in June identified an urgent need for co-ordinated, trauma-informed care for female vets with chronic pain.

items.title: Why Danielle Smith wants to give a subsidy to the oilpatch despite near-record profits
items.summary_auto: The Alberta government is preparing to unveil new subsidies later this month for oil companies to ramp up production to help fill the province’s proposed Pacific Link pipeline to the West Coast.

items.title: Vancouver Island village evacuation orders to remain in place for days after landslide
items.summary_auto: An evacuation order for a number of properties following a landslide in the small village of Zeballos on northwest Vancouver Island is expected to remain in place through Friday, as forecasters warn of further heavy rain for the region.

items.title: Mother testifies police killing of autistic son in Surrey, B.C., left her 'broken'
items.summary_auto: At the coroner's inquest into the death of Chase de Balinhard, mother Crystal de Balinhard described the day he was been killed.

items.title: Premier Doug Ford suggests 'ass whooping' for 2 boys connected to alleged assault of Hamilton cadet leader
items.summary_auto: Ontario Premier Doug Ford commented on an alleged assault in Hamilton, saying the parents of two boys police say were involved should "give your kids a little ass whooping in the wood shed."

items.title: Trump downplays FBI probe into Nvidia chief's affair with alleged spy
items.summary_auto: U.S. President Donald Trump said Monday that the FBI is investigating Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's affair with an alleged Chinese government agent, but said he doesn't think the executive who has helped to develop artificial intelligence has a reason to worry.

items.title: What these newly elected U.S. reps. think about tariffs on Canada
items.summary_auto: Several newly elected Democratic representatives are calling for an end to the U.S.-Canada trade war, citing concerns over rising living costs and job losses.

items.title: ‘A lot of different ideas’: Canada’s sport leaders meet in Ottawa to discuss next steps
items.summary_auto: The Playground to Podium Summit began Monday at the National Arts Centre in Ottawa, bringing together around 400 of Canada's pre-eminent sports leaders with the intention of charting a new path forward for an industry that was in desperate need of a refresh.

items.title: Could Nvidia survive without its ultra-powerful CEO, Jensen Huang?
items.summary_auto: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has helmed the company since starting it in 1993, guiding it from a graphics card maker to the AI behemoth it is today. But with an investigation now underway into whether Huang was the target of a foreign intelligence effort and no clear successor in sight, analysts say a change at the top — if it were deemed necessary — would be massive.

items.title: Canadian astronaut Joshua Kutryk does a Q&A (and a backflip) from space
items.summary_auto: Canadian astronaut Joshua Kutryk answered questions from students in St. John's and showed off life in zero gravity from aboard the International Space Station on Monday.

items.title: Canadian ultramarathoner Stephanie Case is the 1st woman to run 100 miles in Antarctica
items.summary_auto: Canadian ultramarathoner Stephanie Case completed the Antarctic Ice Ultra in Queen Maud Land, Eastern Antarctica, on Sunday, making her the first woman to run 100 miles, or 160.9 kilometres, on the southernmost continent covered by the largest ice sheet in the world.

items.title: 2026 Booker Prize goes to post-apocalyptic, sci-fi novel The End of Everything
items.summary_auto: English author M. John Harrison has won the 2026 Booker Prize for his novel The End of Everything, a post-apocalyptic adventure that explores what it means to be human in a shifting world. It's the first time a science fiction writer has won the annual prize, which honours the best novel written in English.

items.title: A surprise baby right whale spotted near Quebec is bringing 'a lot of hope' for the species
items.summary_auto: Scientists were shocked and delighted to discover a previously unaccounted for baby right whale swimming alongside its mama off the coast of Quebec.

items.title: Ottawa doubles maximum time employer can hire low-wage temporary foreign workers
items.summary_auto: The government said restrictions on hiring temporary foreign workers in cities with unemployment rates above six per cent will remain in place. But Ottawa is adding early childhood educators to the list of professions exempted from those restrictions, which already includes certain jobs in health care, construction and food processing.

items.title: Fact check: Is this a photo of the Poland shooter?
items.summary_auto: The Polish gunman who killed six people in Krakow has been identified as 24-year-old Michal Oksinski. But is that the person shown in this photo circulating online? CBC’s Fact Check team debunks the misinformation.

items.title: Man who used fraudulent passport to get in and out of Canada 16 times handed 2-year sentence
items.summary_auto: A Ghanaian man who used a fraudulent Canadian passport to leave and re-enter the country 16 times has been sentenced to two years in prison for citizenship fraud.

items.title: Tyler Robinson, man accused of shooting Charlie Kirk, to face trial in 2028
items.summary_auto: A ​Utah judge on Monday set a June 2028 trial date for Tyler Robinson, the man accused of murdering prominent right-wing activist Charlie Kirk last year.

items.title: Roshel to buy Stellantis assembly plant in Brampton for undisclosed amount, automaker says
items.summary_auto: Canadian armoured vehicle maker Roshel Inc. will buy the Stellantis assembly plant in Brampton, Ont., the automaker announced Monday.

items.title: Ontario university student pleads not guilty in U.S. court amid Chinese 'espionage' probe
items.summary_auto: An Ontario university student has pleaded not guilty in a U.S. federal court in a case a prosecutor described as involving "espionage-type activities." Weiheng (Billy) Zeng is charged with making false statements following an FBI counter-intelligence investigation.

items.title: Judge clears way for Lindsay Clancy to face potential 2nd trial
items.summary_auto: A Massachusetts judge cleared the way on Monday for Lindsay Clancy to be tried again on murder charges for killing her three young children at her home in 2023, saying a retrial would not unconstitutionally subject ‌her to a double prosecution for the same crime.

items.title: U.S. House Republican moves to force vote on impeaching Pete Hegseth
items.summary_auto: Republican Rep. Thomas Massie moved Monday to force a vote to impeach Secretary of War Pete Hegseth, putting pressure on his fellow Republicans to decide whether to remove one of the Trump administration's most prominent figures following sweeping election losses.

items.title: Like father, like son: Arnold Schwarzenegger’s son muscles into top 5 at bodybuilding competition
items.summary_auto: More than 60 years after Arnold Schwarzenegger first flexed his stuff on a bodybuilding stage, his youngest son is continuing the dynasty of muscle, scoring in the top five during his professional debut over the weekend.

items.title: Payments Canada launches long-delayed instant payments system
items.summary_auto: Payments Canada says it has launched its real-time rail national payment system, which is expected to speed day-to-day payments for Canadian businesses and consumers.

items.title: $276 for hair ties? Skims offers advent calendar refunds after online backlash
items.summary_auto: After intense customer backlash, Kim Kardashian's apparel brand Skims is offering refunds to anyone who purchased its 2026 accessories advent calendar, which costs $276 and was advertised as "12 fun days of surprises."

items.title: Honda Canada announces plans to retool Alliston, Ont., plant for hybrid production
items.summary_auto: Honda Canada says it will retool its manufacturing facilities in Alliston, Ont., to expand production of hybrid-electric and gasoline-powered vehicles. The Japanese automaker announced Monday it is partnering with the federal and provincial governments to fund plant upgrades, including the reintroduction of engine manufacturing, with an initial $166-million investment.

items.title: James Gunn, Peter Safran out of DC Studios as Skydance shakeup continues
items.summary_auto: Skydance Motion Picture Group announced Monday that James Gunn and Peter Safran are stepping down as co-chief executives after four years leading DC Studios.

items.title: Heated Rivalry could be getting 2 more seasons and a movie, sources say
items.summary_auto: Deadline has reported the cast and crew of Heated Rivalry are currently filming not one but two new seasons, and a movie could be scheduled for theatrical release in December 2027.

items.title: Top U.S. hedge fund executive named CEO of Canada's new sovereign wealth fund
items.summary_auto: A top executive at one of the world's largest hedge funds is leaving her job in the U.S. to become the CEO of one of the Carney government's hallmark projects.

items.title: Lionel Messi achieves MLS first, winning Golden Boot for second straight season
items.summary_auto: Lionel Messi has been awarded the 2026 MLS Golden Boot, becoming the first player in league history to win the award in consecutive seasons.
